To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the photocatalytic degradation of organic compounds by quantum-sized semiconductor colloidal suspensions is a complex process that involves the oxidation of surface-bound organic species by valence band and trapped holes as well as by surface-bound hydroxy radicals.

(1) the photocatalytic reaction of acetate on quantum-sized ZnO surfaces is complex and involves the production of many different products; (2) the reaction is initiated by the direct oxidation of adsorbed acetate by valance band holes; (3) the reaction is terminated by the formation of surface-bound hydroxide radicals and subsequent reaction with acetate; (4) the reaction of acetate by hydroxide radicals on the surface of the semiconductor is the rate-limiting step

(a) the photooxidation reaction of organic compounds on semiconductor surfaces is complex and involves a variety of surface intermediates, (b) the reaction products and reaction pathways are dependent upon the nature of the semiconductor and the surface coverage by the electron donor, (c) surface-mediated reactions play a dominant role when electron donors are strongly bound to semiconductor surfaces, and (d) the reaction pathways are dependent on the relative reactivity of the electron donors toward oxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photooxidation reactions of organic molecules adsorbed to the surface of semiconductor particles.
the development of a new class of photocatalysts based on semiconductor colloids.
the development of new methods for the oxidation of organic pollutants in water using semiconductor colloids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidation of organic acids by quantum-sized semiconductor colloidal particles is a complex, multi-step process involving both direct and indirect oxidation mechanisms.
the photocatalytic reactions of organic acids on semiconductor particles are very complex and involve a variety of mechanisms.

the photooxidation products of organic acids on illuminated semiconductor surfaces are determined by both direct oxidation by valence band or trapped holes and by indirect oxidation by surface-bound hydroxy radicals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photocatalytic reaction of a given organic substrate with semiconductor colloids is not a simple one-electron oxidation reaction.

the photooxidation mechanism of organic molecules on quantum-sized ZnO surfaces is a complicated process that depends on the nature of the adsorbed organic species, the concentration of adsorbed species, and the photon flux.

the product distribution observed in the photocatalytic reaction of acetate on ZnO colloids is a function of the relative rates of the following three processes: (1) the adsorption of acetate, (2) the adsorption and reaction of the oxidation products of acetate, and (3) the desorption of the reaction products.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the photooxidation mechanism of organic acids on semiconductor surfaces is more complicated than previously thought, and it is not sufficient to assume that free hydroxyl radical is the only reactive species.
, in order to understand the photocatalysis of complex organic compounds, one must consider not only the oxidation of the primary substrate but also the oxidation of the reaction intermediates.
the product distribution is determined by a competition between the direct oxidation of surface bound acetate and the indirect oxidation by surface-bound hydroxy radical.
